book.title: Primitives: Points Build Worlds
book.source: hand reading (Claude) + 10 hall checkers + workflow reader/skeptic

reading.arc: The simplex built one point at a time and then taken apart: point, segment, triangle, tetrahedron; then what meshes do to those ideas: a cube whose connectivity outlasts its shape, a sphere whose resolution is a distribution rather than a quantity, a torus family that converges without arriving, and finally an arrangement (the pyramid court, Durer's tableau) where knowing how a form is made no longer finishes the looking. The sequence opens on a counter that started before you and closes on the same counter, much larger now: some of the number is yours, a fixed quantity of it never will be, and the number has no field for the difference.
holds: Refrains repeated verbatim across the gap: 'Bring the detour.' closes Lines and opens Trace; 'Look for your bend. It may have grown.' closes Trace and opens Grid. Every one of the ten handovers matches its neighbour, and Melencolia names the next sequence.

The carried drawing: a line drawn in Trace travels to Grid (rescaled) and to Triangle, where it arrives 'made fillable' (six positions of hundreds, flattened, scaled). The pipeline's losses become the lesson.
Instruction versus enforcement: DO NOT CROSS (a collider the explosion removes), WALK THIS LINE (a stripe that scores nothing), the STOP sign with no collision body.

Seeing versus colliding: from 'Seeing it and being able to hold it are different things' to the trihedron whose rendering is open while its physics is closed, to the torus whose extra triangles give it no other hole.

What a display can show: %.2f in Point_One, 'Remember it when we reach Trace and Grid' in Lines, snappedf in Trace, roundi in Grid, a triangle counter that counts a construction without deciding whether it fills the intended region.

hall_notes.note: Refuses to begin: the counter started before you, the origin is a chosen place, the invisible point exists in code before anything is drawn, the card rounds your hand out of the report, the target's tolerance ignores intention. Nine stations; the overture before the first heading is long.
The exploding barrier ('Someone joined those events in code'), b - a, WALK THIS LINE and the walking recorder. 'Two points were enough to begin. They have not made the world small.'

The richest hall: the five-millimetre gate, dots that round to 10/40/80 mm ('Your wrist is negotiating with a spacing'), the stick, the head trace, the writing desk ('We have given waiting a length'), the amber point that forgets.
'The same place has two names.' Snapping, the walking recorder at one-metre spacing, the ruled field, the plan vitrine. Three heavy references on one hall.

The best argument in the sequence: shift the start of a fan around a six-corner L and the fill reaches into the notch. 'The code kept its rule; the rule failed to keep your boundary.' Then: keep the overspill.
Trihedron against tetrahedron; rendering open, physics closed; the pink corner cut into the room; wedges, barrier, STOP.
'What looks like construction is also an arrangement of when we are allowed to see.' Pull v6 and a square becomes two tilted triangles. The crates spell A WORLD WITHOUT COMPOSITION YET.
The Academy motto reversed. Resolution has a distribution (16x16, 7x7, 1x10). The five-sided capsule: 'recognising a capsule was not yet knowing this one.'
Twenty tori, the unit polygon's perimeter, tolerance as a stopping criterion, REVERSE. Achilles at stage ten: 'His visible body is larger than the gap.' Nothing here is a portal.
The court, the snap puzzle that completes its test while the question stays open, the magic square (the sums check), and the counter's return: the best paragraph in the ten chapters.

stumbles: Point_One: 'Alice's rabbit is already ahead' and 'We are already Alice' with no introduction of Alice on page one.
Point_One: the format-cycling label ('One format leaves the body without a printed address') is the one instruction whose lesson is not stated.
Point_One: 'An earlier version confined the point to the arrows' span' is revision history inside the reader's prose.
Point_One: 'Watch for the falling balls' arrives before the balls are introduced.
Point_Lines and Point_Line_Grid: 'On desktop it follows the walker' and 'On desktop, follow the same addresses with your walk' are manual voice; the reader is in the headset.
Point_Line_Grid: 'If the field is empty, return to Trace, draw ... and let go' is troubleshooting inside the chapter.
Point_Triangle_Context: the L procedure is demanding on the page (flat, two equal arms, the guide's timing); the text names corners A-F while the tool shows numbers.
Primitives_Portals: the hall is called Portals and nothing in it is a portal; the footnote has to deny teleportation.
Primitives_Melencolia: 'Ten rooms ago' in the tenth room.

Across the sequence: the closing cadence ('It does not tell us where to stop', 'Geometry does not decide the use', 'It cannot decide which of those things we should want') recurs a dozen times; by Portals the reader can predict a section's last sentence.

keep.quote: Its first number for you is not its first number.
The apparent stillness belongs to the report.
Your intention never enters this comparison.
Thirty-two positions are neither thirty-two seconds nor a fixed length of line.
The code kept its rule; the rule failed to keep your boundary.
enough to hold which distinction, for whom, at what distance?
His visible body is larger than the gap.

The frames that passed before you had somewhere to stand did not become yours by being counted alongside the ones that followed. This number adds them together anyway. It has no field for the difference.

reading.handover_in: First sequence of the spine; no chapter before it. The book opens with an epigraph lifted from the chapter's own middle and "You arrive late."
reading.handover_out: Melencolia closes "In transformation, you can watch from one place as objects move, turn and scale" and hands over a relation to test against change. Trans_Pre is next.
reading_errors: Point_Line_Grid hall note ('carries two desktop asides and one wrong interval count') and the stumble 'the display snaps at a quarter metre': the interval count is not wrong. grid_lines.tscn:8 sets shadow_snap_subdivisions = 6 on the root node (overriding the .gd default of 4), the registry instantiates that scene, and the map token cannot change it; the green trace snaps at 1/6 m and the chapter's 'six intervals per metre' is correct.

'Ahmed's orientation the one theorist carried by name through five halls' footnotes': Ahmed appears in four halls' footnotes — Point_One (ahmed-reach), Point_Lines (ahmed-paths, ahmed-deviation), Point_Line_Grid (ahmed-return) and Primitives_Polythedra (polyhedra-ahmed); Trace, Triangle_Context, Animatedcube, Ignorance, Portals and Melencolia do not name her.

Minor: 'Seven recorders of one gesture' for Point_Trace is a count of rules, not recorders — the hall has six tagged instruments (draw_dot, draw_stick, head_trace_projection, automatic_writing_desk, whiteboard, trace_short_memory) and nine physical recorders (four dots, stick, head, desk, board, cord).

dropped.title: The desk accumulates _t, not _elapsed
dropped.reason: The reader grepped the host script only. Point_Trace places the desk as automatic_writing_desk:0:0#recording:head_height#rows:5#write_speed:0.06#run_demo:0 (Point_Trace/map_data.json), and the chapter's section describes exactly that measured mode ('the height of your headset moves the mark'). In head_height mode automatic_writing_desk.gd:254-255 calls _measured_writer.advance(delta) and returns BEFORE `_t += delta` at :257, so `_t` never accumulates in this hall. The measured writer's clock is commons/primitives/automatic_writing_desk/measured_height_writer.gd:11 (`var _elapsed := 0.0`) and :62 (`_elapsed += delta` in _advance_clock, feeding pen position at :63-65 and the sample times at :120). The chapter quotes the one line that asks for the number in the mode the visitor meets; the identifier exists and is correct. Replacing it with `_t += delta` would make the chapter wrong.
